frames.narration: The nightly job finishes and reports what it did: run r-5521 read two tables and wrote one table called daily_orders. The event goes on the queue, because thousands of jobs finish at the same time.
A writer takes the event. It has not seen r-5521 before, so it adds the two edges to the graph. When the queue delivers the same event a second time, the writer sees the id and does nothing.
The search index learns about the new table from the metadata store, and its dependents count rises, because more jobs now read from it than before.
An engineer wants to rename a column in raw_events, a core table. They ask the catalog what would be affected.

The impact service walks the graph breadth first with a map of visited assets. Seven assets read raw_events directly, 17 are within two hops, and 73 are affected in all, up to eight hops away. A table reached by several routes is counted once.
The 73 assets belong to five teams. The result is grouped by owner and shown to the engineer, who sees that stopping at two hops would have hidden 56 of the affected assets.

The engineer plans the change and the notifier sends each of the five owning teams a message that lists only its own affected assets, with the date of the change and the upstream checks that currently pass.
